issues.description: The exercise asks students to 'Create a constructor that initializes every attribute of the Lecture class' (problem statement) but the reference implementation declares the constructor with package-private visibility (no access modifier). Because the Lecture class itself is public, a non-public constructor prevents code outside the package from instantiating Lecture (for example, tests or users in a different package). This visibility choice is likely unintentional and may confuse students about whether the constructor should be public.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Lecture constructor public in the solution (and suggest students implement a public constructor in the template). Change the constructor signature to 'public Lecture(...)' so the class can be instantiated from other packages (e.g., test code or user code outside the package).
